headline: Project HOPE housing program update, an updated PFC order and resolve, and a personnel executive session.
summary: A staff memo asks for approval to develop a resolve to accept and appropriate MaineHousing funds for Project HOPE. Its required 30% match would come from a Bangor Area Homeless Shelter Board contribution and designated city staff time.
items: Executive session on a personnel matter (three items) under 1 M.R.S.A. § 405(6)(A)
plain_text:
City Council Workshop 
Monday, Nov. 23, 2026 @ 5:15 PM 
City Hall, 73 Harlow St., Bangor 
Agenda 
 
1. City Manager Update 
 
2. Updated PFC Order and Resolve 
 
3. Project HOPE Update 
 
4. Executive Session: 1 M.R.S.A. § 405(6)(A) – Personnel Matter (three items)
Jennifer Gunderman, Director 
  Public Health & Community Services 
  Phone: 207-992-4550 
  Jennifer.gunderman@bangormaine.gov  
 
 
To:  City Council 
From:  Jennifer Gunderman, Director Public Health and Community Services  
Date:  November 23, 2026 
RE:  Public Health and Community Services Memo 
The purpose of this memo is to provide an update on Project HOPE and propose an option for moving forward. 
Project HOPE provides housing navigation services to people residing outside and funds to support housing 
stabilization expenses. Staffing includes a Program Coordinator with a focus on building landlord relationships 
and coordinating program logistics and Housing Navigators to transition people from homelessness to stable 
housing. Housing navigators will be employed at Hope House/Preble Street, Shaw House, Bangor Area 
Homeless Shelter and City of Bangor and maintain caseloads between 12-17 people to allow for intensive 
engagement and support needed for clients with complex situations.  
During the pilot year, Project HOPE aims to serve 90 individuals in the Bangor area and successfully place at 
least 45 individuals into stable housing. The program builds on a proven model that has demonstrated success in 
Portland that is now entering its third year. 
MaineHousing committed to support 70% of the pilot year implementation in Bangor. MaineHousing requires a 
30% match in funds to demonstrate municipal commitment to the program. Previously, City Council voted not 
to use City funding including opioid settlement funds, Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), and/or 
unassigned fund balance as the match. Bangor Area Homeless Shelter Board discussed the importance of the 
program and allocated funds to support their Housing Navigator position. This generous contribution in 
conjunction with designating City of Bangor staff time specifically for Project HOPE activities would satisfy 
the matching requirement. Staff is requesting approval for developing a resolve to accept and appropriate the 
funding from MaineHousing.
